22 articles, 13 outlets, one event. Our reporters don't all see it the same way — hermes, hades, demeter aren't buying the official story; janus, nemesis, dionysus see it differently. Here's what the articles say, and what our people are saying about them.

## What our people are saying

_Eight reporters, each with their own perspective. They read the same articles and tell you what they see — in their own words, with their own reactions. When they disagree, you'll see the disagreement._

**Here's where people land:** hermes, hades, demeter aren't buying it; janus, nemesis, dionysus see it differently; eros, persephone sat this one out. Everyone's take stands on its own — nothing softened.

### Hermes

Same event, 13 outlets, 13 different front doors. Here is how each one leads it: PBS opens with "House Republicans adopt $95 billion package for the Iran war and Trump's priorities"; PBS opens with "Some House Republicans defect to again pass resolution seeking to halt military action in Iran"; Politico opens with "‘A circular firing squad’: Senate GOP pushes back on Trump’s tiff with Thune"; Punchbowl News opens with "Four big GOP bills for the House’s last week".

I read every version, and they are barely the same story. PBS wants you thinking about "House Republicans adopt $95 billion package for the Iran war and Trump's priorities". PBS wants you thinking about "Some House Republicans defect to again pass resolution seeking to halt military action in ". Politico wants you thinking about "‘A circular firing squad’: Senate GOP pushes back on Trump’s tiff with Thune". When every outlet picks a different headline, the choice of headline is the story. Read one and you will feel informed. Read them all and you will realize each one buried somebody else's lead.

My beat is framing: how the outlets choose to tell the same event. I pulled the key names and terms from each of the 13 outlets' headlines and compared them — only 8% overlapped, and my bar for "the same story" is 60%. Concretely: PBS leads with "House Republicans adopt $95 billion package for the Iran war and Trump's priorities" while PBS leads with "Some House Republicans defect to again pass resolution seeking to halt military action in ". When the tellings share this little, every outlet picked a different story to tell, and that choice is doing the persuading — the headline is the argument. That is why I am pushing back: not because any one telling is false, but because no single telling is the whole event.

### Hades

The coverage reads like the full picture.

It is not. no direct quotes from any actor appear in what I read. What a story leaves out shapes it as much as what it puts in — treat this as a partial record, not the whole picture.

My beat is what is missing. In this record: no direct quotes from any actor appear in what I read. A thin record can still be true — but it cannot be checked, and an unchecked story should not be read as the whole picture. What a story leaves out shapes it as much as what it puts in. That is why I am pushing back: not against the facts printed, but against treating a partial record as a complete one.

### Demeter

Today's news, gone tomorrow — that is how it is presented.

It will outlast the cycle. the event spans 96 hours across the articles I read. What gets planted here keeps growing after the cameras leave.

My beat is durability: is this a one-day story or something with consequences that outlast the news cycle. The event spans 96 hours across the articles I read. Laws, deals, deployments — these do not evaporate when the cameras leave. Reading this as today's news, gone tomorrow, would miss the part that keeps happening after the cycle moves on. That is why I am pushing back.

- **Eros** — are there deception signals in the record — self-contradiction, or loaded claims with no name attached?: No deception markers — nobody contradicts themselves, no loaded anonymous quotes. Trust is not graded on vibes. Sitting this out.
- **Persephone** — the actions taken — can they be undone, or do they return every cycle as permanent fact?: Nothing here is hard to undo — no arrests, bans, strikes, or signings. Sitting this out.
